title: Fairness-Regularized DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails, handles and IP addresses with placeholders, and tokenizes dynamically with the DeBERTa-v3-small tokenizer to 128 tokens. A pretrained encoder is mean-pooled over attended tokens, followed by dropout, projection, layer normalization, GELU and a toxicity logit head; optional subtype and identity heads are added. Identity prediction uses gradient reversal to encourage identity-invariant shared features. Training uses normalized sample and annotation-confidence weights, combining soft and hard toxicity BCE, masked subtype BCE, adversarial identity BCE, and a conditional squared-correlation penalty between toxicity probabilities and identity labels within positive and negative toxicity groups. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates, no decay for bias or normalization parameters, warm-up then cosine decay, mixed precision, accumulation, and gradient clipping. Adversarial and decorrelation weights ramp during early updates. Inference disables reversal, dynamically pads batches, and applies sigmoid to toxicity logits.

title: Evidence-Gated ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are cleaned, HTML-unescaped, and normalized; emails and URLs are replaced, and long text is head-tail truncated. A heuristic focus view selects salient clauses using identity, hostility, threat, support, second-person, and punctuation cues. Standardized clipped numeric features capture text statistics, lexicon matches, identity counts, and identity-hostility proximity. A partially unfrozen pretrained ModernBERT encodes separately packed context and focus segments marked by added tokens. Attention pooling produces region vectors, which are combined with an MLP numeric embedding, absolute differences, and products. A context logit is adjusted by a gated focus delta; joint features predict toxicity subtypes and beta-binomial concentration. Training uses confidence-, subgroup-, rarity-, and annotator-informed weighted soft-target BCE, with optional beta-binomial, masked subtype, worst identity-toxicity-cell, and gate regularization losses. AdamW, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, and cosine scheduling optimize the model. Evaluation returns clipped toxicity probabilities.

title: Dual-view counterfactual toxicity classifier
summary: The system splits toxicity comments into training and validation data, cleans Unicode/HTML/control text, replaces URLs and emails, and constructs an identity-masked counterfactual view. It derives standardized numeric text and identity-context features, continuous toxicity targets, masked auxiliary toxicity/identity targets, and normalized identity-aware sample weights. A pretrained ModernBERT encoder processes original and masked tokenized comments; only its top four layers and normalization modules are trainable. Mean-pooled 384-dimensional view representations are fused with an MLP embedding of numeric features, their mean, absolute difference, and agreement. Averaged branch logits produce toxicity predictions, while an auxiliary multilabel head uses original, mean-view, and numeric representations. The loss combines weighted soft-label BCE, auxiliary BCE, symmetric Bernoulli-KL view consistency, and identity-partition pairwise ranking losses. AdamW uses separate encoder/head rates, cosine warmup, mixed precision, accumulation, finite-loss checks, and gradient clipping. Inference sigmoids and clips the averaged dual-view logit.

title: Dual-View Counterfactual ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The pipeline cleans comments, forms an identity-masked counterfactual view, and derives scaled numeric text, lexical, identity, and style features. Original and masked texts are jointly tokenized to 128 tokens and processed by ModernBERT, with only its top two transformer layers and named normalization modules trainable. Mean-pooled view embeddings are projected to 256 dimensions and numeric features use a 48-dimensional MLP. Toxicity prediction combines both views, their mean, absolute difference, agreement, and numeric features; the final logit averages view logits. An auxiliary identity head uses original, mean-view, and numeric representations. Training uses weighted toxicity and per-view BCE, view-consistency KL, masked auxiliary BCE, and identity-partition ranking losses. AdamW uses separate encoder and head rates, cosine warmup, mixed precision, accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities.

title: Evidence-Focused ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution preprocesses comments by HTML/control cleanup, email/URL masking, lexicon-based identity and hostility analysis, and construction of context, analysis, and clause-selected focus views. It standardizes clipped style, lexical, identity, proximity, and identity-specific numeric features using training data only, and forms continuous/thresholded toxicity and masked auxiliary labels. A ModernBERT-large model receives packed, separately budgeted context and focus text plus numeric features. It attention-pools both regions, encodes numeric inputs with an MLP, models vector interactions, and adjusts a context toxicity logit through a gated focus delta; it also predicts beta-binomial concentration and optional subtypes. The composite loss includes weighted toxicity BCE, optional annotator-count beta-binomial likelihood, masked subtype BCE, worst identity/toxicity-cell loss, and gate regularization. Identity-aware sampling balances identity/toxicity cells. Training freezes lower encoder layers, uses AdamW, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference uses deterministic loaders and clipped probabilities.

title: Dual-View ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution trains a dual-view toxicity classifier on original comments and identity-masked counterfactual versions. Text is Unicode/HTML-normalized; URLs and emails are replaced, identity terms are masked, and scaled text-statistic and binary lexical/context features are computed. Toxicity and identity annotations become masked auxiliary targets, with missing values zero-filled after validity masks are recorded. A shared ModernBERT encoder mean-pools token states; only its top four layers and direct normalization modules are fine-tuned. Numeric features pass through a two-layer MLP. Representations from both views, their mean, absolute difference and product are combined for toxicity and auxiliary heads. The final toxicity logit averages per-view logits. Losses include weighted primary and per-view BCE, symmetric Bernoulli-KL consistency, masked weighted auxiliary BCE, and softplus-margin ranking losses over identity subgroup partitions. AdamW, warmup-plus-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping are used. Inference sigmoid-transforms and clips averaged logits.

title: Evidence-Focused ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system cleans comments, creates head-tail context and lexicon-scored focus clauses, and derives standardized, clipped numeric text and identity features using training-only fitting. It packs separately truncated context and focus tokens with learned marker tokens for a partially unfrozen ModernBERT encoder. Masked pools for both regions, numeric-feature embeddings, their difference, and product feed interaction layers. Toxicity is predicted as a context logit plus a gated focus adjustment; optional subtype logits and beta-binomial vote concentration are also produced. The loss combines confidence- and subgroup-weighted soft-label BCE, optional vote likelihood, masked subtype BCE, worst identity/toxicity-cell loss, and gate regularization. Fairness-oriented sampling rotates across identity/background and toxic/non-toxic cells. AdamW uses differentiated backbone/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference preserves input order and clips probabilities; checkpoints include model, tokenizer, scaler, preprocessing metadata, and training state.

title: DeBERTa Ordinal Toxicity Prediction Pipeline
summary: The pipeline normalizes comment text, separates quoted speech, replaces URLs/emails with markers, and builds a model-text view. It extracts 29 handcrafted linguistic features and duplicate-hash statistics; training duplicate priors use leave-one-out smoothing, while validation/test use training-derived statistics. Features are standardized on training data. A partially fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large encoder combines CLS, learned masked attention pooling, and an MLP over numeric features. A fusion network produces monotonic 19-threshold ordinal outputs, binary and fractional toxicity outputs, and optional auxiliary labels. Loss combines confidence-weighted ordinal and binary BCE, Smooth-L1 regression, auxiliary BCE, and identity-stratified pairwise ranking. Sampling with replacement upweights toxic and identity cases; text is occasionally replaced by the clean view. Long sequences retain head and tail portions. AdamW uses layer-wise backbone decay, separate head rates, warm-up/cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference uses model-text predictions clipped to [0,1].

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Fairness Regularization
summary: The solution normalizes comments, masks URLs, emails, handles and IP addresses, and tokenizes text with a DeBERTa-v3-small tokenizer using length 128 and dynamic padding. It predicts toxicity from mean-pooled transformer features processed by dropout, projection, layer normalization and GELU; optional subtype and identity heads use available masked labels. Training weights upweight toxic and identity-related examples, including non-toxic identity mentions and rarer groups, and incorporate normalized annotator-count confidence. The loss combines weighted BCE for continuous and thresholded toxicity targets, masked subtype BCE, gradient-reversed identity BCE, and class-conditional toxicity–identity correlation penalties. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates and excludes bias and normalization parameters from weight decay. AMP training uses shuffled batches, accumulation, clipping, warmup-cosine scheduling, and ramped adversarial/fairness terms. Inference disables gradient reversal and applies sigmoid to toxicity logits; checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, configuration and training state.

title: Sparse Wide-Deep Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text and replaces URLs, emails, handles and IP addresses with markers. It combines standardized dense stylistic, lexical and identity-related features with L2-normalized hashed word 1–2 gram and character 3–5 gram CSR features. Sparse embedding bags produce wide scalars and deep vectors; dense features encode gating signals for word and character views. Gated vectors are fused, normalized, processed by a low-rank nonlinear cross layer and context encoder, then scored with a deep toxicity head plus scaled wide scores. Optional subtype heads use context features. An identity classifier receives gradient-reversed crossed features. Training uses weighted toxicity BCE with soft and hard targets, masked subtype BCE, adversarial identity BCE, conditional within-class identity–toxicity correlation penalties, and wide-logit regularization. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam and other parameters AdamW, with warm-up/cosine schedules, adversarial-loss ramps, and dense-gradient clipping. Inference disables reversal and sigmoid-transforms toxicity logits.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are cleaned by Unicode/HTML normalization and replacement of URLs, emails and IPs, then represented by tokenized text and 22 standardized style/lexicon features. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder pools CLS and masked mean embeddings, fuses projected non-identity numeric features, and outputs toxicity and subtype logits. A gradient-reversal identity head discourages identity information in the fused representation. Training combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked subtype BCE, adversarial identity BCE, overall and subgroup/background ranking losses with smooth worst-group aggregation, plus optional masked-identity counterfactual BCE and logit-consistency loss. Fairness batches sample an identity and its toxic/non-toxic subgroup and background pools; ordinary and fairness batches alternate. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. At inference, identity-lexicon rows whose masked text changes are scored twice and blend original and masked logits before sigmoid clipping.

title: Identity-aware multi-view toxicity classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments and creates original, identity-abstracted, and identity-counterfactual text views. It extracts 32 standardized, clipped numeric features and constructs soft toxicity, subtype, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP targets with identity-aware sample weights. Abstracted text is processed by a partially fine-tuned ModernBERT encoder, while original and counterfactual UTF-8 byte sequences are processed by dilated depthwise-convolution encoders; numeric features use an MLP. Gated fusion combines semantic and style representations. The model produces a main toxicity logit, original- and counterfactual-view auxiliary logits, and optional masked subtype predictions. Its loss combines weighted soft-label BCE, smooth-max class-balanced metric-cell loss, auxiliary-view BCE, subtype BCE, and counterfactual consistency. Training uses AdamW with backbone/head parameter groups, warm-up and cosine learning-rate decay, mixed precision, and gradient clipping. Inference blends sigmoid probabilities from the three toxicity logits using 0.80, 0.10, and 0.10 weights.

title: Sparse Wide-Deep Toxicity Predictor
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails, mentions and obfuscated profanity, and derives stylometric, toxic-term, identity-term, frequency and smoothed target-history features. Text uses training-fitted hashed word unigram/bigram TF-IDF features; numeric features are standardized from training data. Samples are weighted by clipped inverse-square-root target/identity cell frequency. A sparse wide embedding yields a bag-level logit, while sparse context embeddings and encoded numeric features are fused by a sigmoid gate, interaction and shared GELU/dropout MLP. The final toxicity logit combines scaled wide and residual logits; optional subtype heads use available labels. Training uses weighted BCE for fractional toxicity, masked subtype BCE, global pairwise ranking, and smooth worst-slice ranking losses over identity-defined groups, with deterministic pair caps. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam and remaining parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Batched inference returns clipped sigmoid probabilities. Checkpoints store weights, configuration, feature schema and preprocessing state.

title: Lexicon-Guided Weak-Span Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are split externally, normalized, and augmented with standardized style features, identity indicators, and lexicon-derived toxic-evidence text. A binary training vocabulary estimates smoothed term log-odds from soft toxicity labels; high-evidence sentences, identity context, and truncated original text form model input. A ModernBERT-large encoder freezes lower layers while fine-tuning its final six layers and normalization. CLS and learned attention pooling produce toxicity and identity representations; numeric features are fused through an MLP. Toxicity combines a global logit with gated top-k token-span evidence, with subtype, identity, and uncertainty heads. Training uses fractional targets and weights reflecting subgroup/rarity, certainty, and annotator reliability. The objective includes weighted BCE and configurable beta-binomial, robust subgroup, global/span, masked auxiliary, orthogonality, and concentration terms. AdamW, layer-wise learning rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation, clipping, and length-bucketed batches are used. Batched evaluation returns clipped sigmoid probabilities and auxiliary outputs; checkpoints retain trainable state and preprocessing metadata.

title: Quote-Aware Evidential DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comment text, detects block, line and inline quotations, marks author and quoted spans, and derives clipped text, discourse and identity features separately by span. It trains a DeBERTa-v3-large model with added span tokens; valid token states are attention-pooled for author and quote content, fused with selected numeric features, and passed to toxicity and optional subtype heads. A concentration head outputs bounded Beta parameters using fused and numeric features. Supervision uses soft toxicity labels, masked subtype labels, annotation counts and confidence/identity-derived weights. Loss combines weighted soft-label BCE, beta-binomial likelihood, masked subtype BCE, quote-removal consistency for qualifying examples, and author/quote representation-similarity regularization. Only the final four backbone layers are trainable. A shuffled round-robin sampler balances identity-mention and binary-toxicity cells. AdamW, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warmup and inverse-square-root decay are used. Inference returns clipped toxicity probabilities; checkpoints retain trainable weights, special embeddings, tokenizer and preprocessing artifacts.

title: History-Augmented Sparse Toxicity Network
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, builds stylometric features, hashed word unigram/bigram TF-IDF features, and head-tail hashed character 3–5-gram features. It adds normalized-text repetition statistics and leave-one-out smoothed target histories for training, with training-derived aggregates for validation/test. Numeric features are training-standardized. A neural model combines sparse word and character EmbeddingBag wide logits with normalized lexical embeddings, a GELU/dropout numeric encoder, gated lexical features, lexical-numeric interactions, and an MLP residual logit; an optional head predicts subtypes. It uses weighted fractional-label BCE, masked subtype BCE, global ranking loss, and smooth worst-slice ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP identity cells. Batches reserve identity/target-cell examples alongside uniform rows. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam and remaining parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Evaluation outputs clipped toxicity probabilities and computes overall and identity-slice AUCs.

title: Adversarial ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails and IPs with tokens, removes artifacts, and derives standardized non-identity numeric text features. It uses runtime splits, weighted examples emphasizing toxicity and identity-related cases, and optional identity-term masking for counterfactual inputs. A partially unfrozen ModernBERT-large encodes 256-token text; CLS and masked-mean embeddings are projected and fused with projected numeric features. Heads predict toxicity and subtypes, while a gradient-reversal head predicts identity labels adversarially. Training combines weighted toxicity BCE, ranking losses for overall and subgroup/background cases, smooth worst-group aggregation, masked class-weighted subtype/identity BCE, and counterfactual BCE plus logit consistency. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, finite-loss checks and gradient clipping. Evaluation tokenizes text, applies sigmoid and clips probabilities. Checkpoints retain trainable parameters, preprocessing, tokenizer, scaler and retained feature indices.

title: Fairness-Aware Dual-Hash Wide-Deep Toxicity Model
summary: Text is identity-neutralized by removing listed identity lexemes, replacing URLs, truncating long comments with a gap marker, and adding punctuation, length, URL and non-ASCII features. Word 1–2-grams and boundary character 3–5-grams are hashed into normalized sparse inputs. Weighted word and character embedding bags produce a wide logit and latent features for a LayerNorm MLP that outputs toxicity plus six subtype logits. Batches combine ordinary examples with quota-balanced toxic/non-toxic subgroup and background examples across selected identities, using clipped inverse-square-root prevalence sampling. The objective combines weighted BCE on smoothed toxicity targets, masked subtype BCE, and capped pairwise softplus ranking losses for subgroup/background comparisons, including a smooth worst-group identity term. SparseAdam updates embedding tables and AdamW updates remaining parameters, with dense-gradient clipping. Batched validation/test inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits and clamps probabilities; runtime code handles split, checkpointing, stopping and submission export.

title: Quote-Aware Evidential Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are cleaned and tagged for author and quoted spans, then represented with scaled text, discourse, quotation and identity-related numeric features. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder with added discourse tokens pools author and quote tokens separately using learned masked attention. Projected author, gated quote, interaction and difference vectors are fused with selected numeric features for dropout-averaged toxicity and subtype predictions; an author-only branch provides a counterfactual prediction. A detached fused representation and numeric features parameterize Beta evidence, with its mean used as toxicity probability. Training combines weighted soft-label BCE, beta-binomial annotation-count likelihood, masked subtype BCE, quote-invariance and representation-separation losses. Identity/toxicity-stratified sampling, AdamW, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, warmup followed by inverse-square-root decay, and cached evaluation inputs are used. Inference clips output probabilities.

title: Evidence-Augmented Weak-Span ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, derives style features, and builds training-only term log-odds evidence scores to select toxic and identity-context sentences alongside truncated full text. It upweights identity subgroup samples, rare subgroup negatives, confident targets, and reliable annotator counts. A partly frozen ModernBERT-large encoder combines CLS and learned attention pooling; toxicity and identity representations are separated, with scaled numeric features fused into toxicity prediction. The toxicity logit combines a global head with a gated local-span score from top-eight non-special token logits. Auxiliary heads predict concentration, toxicity subtypes, and identities. The loss includes weighted soft BCE, optional beta-binomial likelihood, smooth worst-cell subgroup loss, global/span and masked multilabel auxiliary BCE, representation decorrelation, and concentration regularization. Training uses length-bucketed batches, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, AdamW with layer-wise learning rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, and selective weight decay. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Sparse Wide-Deep Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, handles entities and obfuscated profanity, and builds stylometric, toxic/identity-term, text-history, and standardized numeric features. Text uses training-fitted IDF and L2-normalized sublinear hashed word/bigram TF features in a 2^20 sparse space. Repeat-text histories use leave-one-out training values and smoothed priors. Metric-aware sample weights derive from target and identity-cell frequencies. A sparse EmbeddingBag wide branch produces a linear toxicity logit; a context EmbeddingBag is normalized and gated by a numeric LayerNorm/GELU/dropout encoder. Their numeric, gated, and interaction features feed a residual trunk producing toxicity and optional subtype logits. Training combines weighted soft-label BCE, masked subtype BCE, and capped pairwise ranking losses for overall and identity, BPSN, and BNSP comparisons, with smooth worst-slice identity aggregation. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam; other parameters use AdamW with dense gradient clipping. Identity-cell quota batches provide coverage. Inference batches probabilities in evaluation mode and clips outputs.

title: Quote-Aware Evidential DeBERTa Toxicity Model
summary: Comments are normalized into author and quoted spans with discourse markers, while numeric text, quotation, discourse and identity-mention features are standardized using training data. Targets include soft toxicity, masked subtype labels, annotation counts and confidence-based weights. A DeBERTa-v3-large backbone fine-tunes its last four layers. Learned masked-attention pools separately summarize author and quote tokens; projected author, gated quote, interaction and numeric features feed toxicity, author-only counterfactual and subtype heads. A concentration head parameterizes a Beta distribution from detached fused representations and numeric features. The loss combines weighted soft-label BCE, beta-binomial likelihood, masked subtype BCE, non-toxic quote-invariance and author/quote representation-separation terms. Training interleaves identity/toxicity strata and uses AdamW, mixed precision, accumulation, gradient clipping, warmup and inverse-square-root decay. Validation and test inference use cached fixed-length tokenized inputs and clipped probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes and tokenizes comment text, optionally masks identity terms, and derives standardized non-identity numeric text features. It builds identity-by-toxicity pools and alternates ordinary batches with fairness batches sampled from eligible identities and four subgroup/background toxicity pools. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT-large backbone pools CLS and masked mean embeddings, fuses projected numeric features, and predicts toxicity and subtypes. A gradient-reversal identity head promotes identity-invariant representations. Training uses clipped weighted toxicity BCE, overall and subgroup/background pairwise ranking losses with worst-group bias aggregation, masked class-weighted subtype BCE, and adversarial identity BCE. Masked counterfactual views can receive target BCE and logit consistency loss. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup and cosine decay, AMP, accumulation, clipping, and checkpointing. Inference applies sigmoid to validated, clipped toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: A DeBERTa-v3-large classifier predicts toxicity from normalized text, with URLs/emails replaced, HTML/control characters removed, and identity-neutral counterfactual text created by identity-term replacement. It derives lexical/style features, though their use by the neural model is not shown. Lower encoder layers are frozen while six final layers are trainable. Learned masked-attention pooling and CLS pooling are gated, normalized, GELU-projected, and classified using mean logits from three dropout passes. Batches combine shuffled examples with rotating-identity subgroup/background toxic and non-toxic anchors. Text may be replaced by neutral counterparts, and selected paired texts receive Smooth-L1 logit-consistency loss. The objective combines batch-normalized weighted BCE, pairwise differentiable fairness-AUC losses with smooth worst-group aggregation, and counterfactual consistency. Tokenization uses a 192-token limit, dynamic padding and padding multiples of eight. AdamW uses separate backbone/head settings, mixed precision, gradient clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Inference returns sigmoid probabilities in input order.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Ranker with Numeric Residual
summary: The solution uses a runtime-managed train/validation/test split of toxicity comments. Text is NFKC-normalized, with URLs, emails and mentions replaced by placeholders, whitespace cleaned, and empty text mapped to a token. Standardized numeric features encode text form, lexical cues, identity lexicons and identity-context interactions; their scaler is fitted on training data only. Fractional toxicity labels are optimized directly with mean binary cross-entropy with logits. A pretrained ModernBERT classifier produces a text logit, augmented by a LayerNorm-normalized MLP numeric tower with a zero-initialized scalar output. Most encoder parameters are frozen initially, retaining resolved top layers and final normalization modules, with full unfreezing as a compatibility fallback. Training uses deterministic shuffling, AdamW parameter groups, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine learning rates. Batched inference applies sigmoid, reducing batch size after CUDA memory errors. Finalization exports runtime-managed validation and submission outputs.

title: Hybrid Sparse Contextual Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution cleans comments with Unicode/HTML normalization, URL/email masking and whitespace cleanup. It builds standardized, clipped dense style/lexical features and hashed CSR sparse word, character and identity-context n-grams. EmbeddingBag branches encode content, identity context and wide features; residual MLP towers and an identity-content interaction produce toxicity logits. Auxiliary heads predict toxicity subtypes and identity labels, while gradient reversal trains an identity adversary from content features. Training uses weighted BCE on clipped soft toxicity targets, masked auxiliary BCE, subgroup/BPSN/BNSP pairwise ranking losses with smooth worst-group aggregation and optional FIFO partition memory, and adversarial BCE on background-negative rows. Batches replay examples from identity-target partitions. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam and other parameters AdamW, with warm-up/cosine schedules, increasing adversarial scale, gradient controls and skipped non-finite updates. Inference applies the saved feature pipeline, predicts in batches, and clips probabilities.

title: Adaptive Identity-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails and mentions with markers, and creates standardized numeric features from text statistics, lexical cues, identity matches and interactions. A ModernBERT-large classifier combines a partially unfrozen text encoder with a LayerNorm/GELU/dropout numeric residual tower whose zero-initialized output initially preserves the text logit. Soft fractional toxicity labels are optimized with BCE-with-logits. Training batches contain four general examples and background/subgroup negative/positive examples for one round-robin identity. Three pairwise softplus ranking losses compare subgroup and background label cells; together with BCE, they are weighted by adaptive identity-family coefficients updated from loss EMAs, sampling-probability correction, clipped multiplicative steps, and bounded-simplex projection. AdamW uses separate encoder/head rates, selective weight decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation and clipping. Inference dynamically tokenizes text, applies sigmoid to logits, retries CUDA OOM with smaller batches, and exports finite float32 probabilities. Checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, numeric preprocessing and adaptive-loss state.

title: Fairness-Aware Transformer Toxicity Classification
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, creates identity-neutral counterfactual variants, and standardizes numeric text features using training-data statistics. A pretrained sequence classifier is fine-tuned with configurable encoder-layer freezing; supported model variants include masked attention pooling, gated first-token fusion, projection, and dropout-averaged logits. Batches rotate identity groups and include subgroup and background toxicity anchors. The loss combines weighted binary cross-entropy, identity-wise pairwise softplus ranking losses with smooth worst-group aggregation, and weighted Smooth L1 consistency between original and neutralized logits. FIFO fairness-memory queues provide age-decayed opposite-class logits for sparse pair construction. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates, mixed precision, gradient unscaling and norm clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. State, memory, and scheduler advance only after executed optimizer updates. Inference produces toxicity probabilities with sigmoid, validates submission structure and ordering, and saves fairness diagnostics.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Bias-Aware Ranking
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, creates standardized numeric features from stylistic, lexical, identity, and identity-context cues, and retains fractional toxicity targets. It builds per-identity pools for subgroup/background and positive/negative cells. A ModernBERT-large text classifier is combined with a numeric residual tower: two GELU/dropout layers produce a scalar correction added to the text logit, with its final layer zero-initialized. Most encoder layers are frozen; configured top layers, final normalization, and heads are trainable. Batches contain four general examples plus four identity-cell examples selected round-robin. The objective equally weights soft BCE on general examples and logistic pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP comparisons. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates, selective weight decay, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, linear warmup, and cosine decay. Inference tokenizes to 384 tokens, applies sigmoid to logits, and reduces batch size after CUDA out-of-memory errors.

title: Fairness-Regularized Toxicity Transformer
summary: The solution preprocesses comments by normalizing text, masking URLs/emails, removing HTML/control characters, and creating identity-neutralized variants. It adds standardized lexical features and training-derived length buckets, then computes identity-aware sample weights and neutralization probabilities. A pretrained RoBERTa toxicity encoder is fine-tuned with only the upper encoder layers and classifier head trainable. The model produces a toxicity logit using encoder representations, gated attention/CLS pooling, projection, and multi-sample dropout. Batches combine ordinary examples with subgroup/background toxic and non-toxic fairness anchors; altered examples may use original or neutral text and tokenize the counterpart for consistency training. The objective combines weighted binary cross-entropy, subgroup-oriented pairwise ranking losses aggregated by a smoothed worst-group operator, and weighted Smooth-L1 counterfactual consistency. AdamW uses separate backbone/head settings, mixed precision, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Inference returns sigmoid-transformed logits; checkpoints include trainable state, tokenizer, metadata, and probe predictions.

title: Sparse Contextual Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized into hashed word, character, and identity-context n-gram features with standardized, clipped dense style and lexicon/context features. Sparse embedding-bag encoders and dense-feature subsets feed separate content and identity residual GELU MLP towers. Toxicity combines content, content–identity interaction, and sparse wide linear logits. Auxiliary heads use available masked annotations, while a gradient-reversal adversary predicts identities from content representations. The objective combines weighted BCE on clipped soft toxicity labels, masked auxiliary BCE, identity-adversary BCE for eligible non-toxic examples, and temperature-scaled pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP partitions, aggregated with smooth worst-group log-sum-exp. Batches replay identity/target partitions. Sparse parameters use SparseAdam and remaining parameters AdamW; learning rates warm up then decay cosinely. Adversarial strength ramps during training; non-finite losses are skipped and gradients are clipped. Inference disables adversarial scaling and clips probabilities.

title: ModernBERT toxicity classifier with numeric fusion and ranking loss
summary: Comments are normalized by Unicode/HTML cleanup, control-character removal and whitespace collapse, with an empty-text marker. Eighteen deterministic text features are computed and standardized from training data. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder processes right-truncated 256-token inputs; CLS and attention-mask mean-pooled representations are combined, projected, fused with projected numeric features, and classified with one toxicity logit. Fractional toxicity labels are clipped and trained using weighted binary cross-entropy; identity-cell balancing weights use inverse square-root toxic/non-toxic cell frequencies. A training-only ranking term uses bounded CPU FP16 FIFO embedding banks for global and identity-membership/hard-label cells. It estimates smooth pairwise AUCs and aggregates overall, subgroup, and cross-group AUCs with a negative-power mean. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, warm-up, accumulation, mixed precision, gradient clipping, and decoupled weight decay exclusions. After successful updates, detached embeddings are added to banks. Inference applies sigmoid and clips predictions to [0,1].

title: Fairness-Aware Prompted DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The pipeline normalizes comment text, replaces emails, URLs and mentions with special tokens, and fits preprocessing on a train/validation split. It adds standardized text statistics and duplicate-frequency features. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large backbone is frozen except for its final encoder block. Identity-term spans select learned low-rank prompt embeddings injected before that block. First-token and masked-mean representations are concatenated, projected, and combined with projected numeric features for toxicity prediction; subtype and gradient-reversed identity heads are auxiliary. Training uses toxicity BCE, masked subtype and identity BCE, and temperature-scaled subgroup and cross-group pairwise ranking losses. Batches interleave natural samples with available subgroup/background toxicity-cell hard batches. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, gradient accumulation and clipping. Validation aggregates overall and group AUCs by a negative-power mean. Inference tokenizes text, applies sigmoid toxicity probabilities, and clips outputs to [0,1].

title: ModernBERT Cell-Aware Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text and derives 18 deterministic numeric features for length, casing, punctuation, URLs, mentions, and lexicon/context counts. Features are standardized from training data. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder processes right-padded, truncated 256-token comments; first-token and masked mean-pooled representations are fused, projected with numeric features, and classified by a LayerNorm, GELU, dropout head into one toxicity logit. Fractional toxicity targets use weighted binary cross-entropy; weights balance thresholded toxicity across nine identity groups. A CPU FP16 FIFO bank stores detached fused embeddings, hard labels, and identity cells. After warm-up and adequate bank occupancy, optimizer-update boundaries add a differentiable cell-aware pairwise AUC surrogate covering overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP terms with negative-power aggregation. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, clipping, and linear warm-up. Inference returns clipped sigmoid probabilities; the best validation-metric checkpoint is selected for prediction export.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Numeric Features
summary: A toxicity model predicts a fractional probability from normalized comment text and 18 engineered numeric features. Text undergoes Unicode/HTML normalization, control-character removal and whitespace cleanup; blank text becomes [EMPTY]. Features capture text length, casing, punctuation, URLs, mentions, lexicon counts and interactions, then use a training-fitted StandardScaler. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder receives right-truncated sequences of up to 256 tokens. Its CLS and attention-mask mean-pooled embeddings are concatenated and projected; projected numeric features are fused with them in an MLP that outputs one logit. Training uses clipped, mean-normalized sample weights balancing toxicity cells within thresholded identity groups and weighted BCE-with-logits normalized by batch weight. AdamW separates encoder and head learning rates, excludes bias/normalization weights from decay, and uses warm-up, mixed precision, gradient accumulation and clipping. Inference applies sigmoid, finite-value checks and clipping to [0,1].

title: Dual-View DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replacing emails, URLs and mentions with added special tokens, and creates an identity-masked view by replacing lexicon-matched identity terms. It derives standardized text, lexicon and duplicate-frequency features. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes both views; first-token and masked-mean states are projected, fused with their absolute difference and optional numeric features, and scored through a gated residual toxicity head. Auxiliary subtype and identity heads use original and masked views respectively, with gradient reversal for identity prediction. Training freezes lower encoder components, uses AdamW parameter groups, mixed precision, checkpointing, accumulation, clipping, warm-up and cosine decay. Losses combine final/view BCE, view-consistency Smooth-L1, masked auxiliary BCE, and subgroup, BPSN and BNSP ranking losses. Natural batches are interleaved with subgroup-balanced hard batches. Inference returns clipped sigmoid probabilities and checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, preprocessing and schema.

title: Identity-orthogonal ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, engineers standardized text-derived numeric features, and creates case-preserving identity-swap counterfactuals for eligible training comments. A pretrained ModernBERT classifier pools the first-token representation; most backbone weights are frozen while the final four layers and final normalization are fine-tuned. It learns an orthogonal identity basis and removes identity projections from the toxicity representation, while retaining text features for subtype and identity heads. An MLP encodes numeric features and fuses them with text features. The model predicts toxicity with multi-sample dropout and auxiliary subtype and identity outputs. Its loss combines soft and thresholded toxicity BCE, masked subtype/identity BCE, counterfactual consistency Smooth-L1 loss, and basis-orthogonality regularization. AdamW uses parameter groups, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference tokenizes text, combines numeric features, applies sigmoid to toxicity logits, and clips outputs to [0,1].

title: Identity-Orthogonal ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized, cleaned, and replaced with placeholders for structural text patterns. Standardized numeric features capture text statistics and lexical, identity, and interaction patterns; training-only text frequencies and scaling prevent split leakage. The model combines tokenized ModernBERT text with numeric features. Only the final four backbone layers and final normalization are trainable. A learned orthonormal identity basis is projected out of the first-token representation for toxicity prediction, while original representations support identity and subtype heads. Multiple dropout toxicity heads are averaged. Identity-term comments may receive swapped-identity counterfactual texts; their numeric features are duplicated. Losses include soft and thresholded toxicity BCE, masked subtype and identity BCE with increased evaluated-identity weighting, counterfactual consistency for toxicity and subtypes, and basis orthogonality regularization. AdamW uses grouped learning rates/decay, AMP, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.
